title: ephemeral-route-rescue-and-rate-trim-adaptive-hotfix
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Hotfix: add ephemeral route rescue to prevent long-lived sticky circuit flips under cross-region surge; adaptive per-route rate trimming reduces tail latency and reduces SLO violations during bursty regional failovers.
description:
Motivation: During a regional egress disruption we observed a recurring pattern where long-lived sticky route allocations would hold on to overloaded pools and cause cascading circuit flips and extended SLO violations for a subset of customers. This hotfix introduces an ephemeral route-rescue path and a conservative, adaptive rate-trim step to reduce tail latency and stabilize SLOs while a full rollout of the regional failover redesign is scheduled.

What this PR does:
- Introduces a Route Rescue controller that temporarily isolates and re-routes traffic for routes that repeatedly trigger circuit transitions in >3 attempts within a 30s window. The controller marks those routes as "ephemeral-rescue" and applies softer token-level rate trimming plus an accelerated cooldown to allow KV cache transfer.
- Adds an adaptive rate-trim heuristic to the request router that measures per-route token emission bursts and reduces token allotment (max_concurrent_tokens) by up to 30% under sustained tail pressure; trims are decayable and tracked per-tenant-route.
- Improves healthprobe hedging to probe alternate regions faster when a rescue is active to avoid sticky failback.
- Conservative telemetry: adds a new metric rescue_attempts_total and rescue_active_routes, plus tagging to existing slo_violation counters so we can correlate rescue activity with downstream SLO behavior.

Commits summary: single-squash for merge with the following logical commits:
- feat(router): add ephemeral route-rescue controller and state machine
- feat(router): adaptive rate-trim heuristic + config knobs
- perf(healthprobe): faster alternate-region probe when rescue active
- infra(metrics): expose rescue and trimmed_token metrics to statsd
- test: unit + integration coverage for rescue/trim behavior
- docs: brief runbook note in ops/incident-guides about rescue behavior

Files changed (high level):
- services/router/route_rescue.go -- controller and state machine with comments explaining decision thresholds
- services/router/rate_trim.go -- adaptive trim implementation and decay logic
- services/router/router_config.yaml -- new flags (rescue.enabled, rescue.window_seconds, rate_trim.max_pct)
- infra/metrics/rescue_metrics.go -- metrics + tagging
- pkg/healthprobe/hedged_probe.go -- alternate-region probe path when rescue active
- tests/router/rescue_test.go -- unit and table tests for edge cases
- docs/ops/route-rescue.md -- short runbook

Notes on approach and tradeoffs:
- This is intentionally conservative: rescue state duration is short (default 45s) and trims are capped at 30% to avoid harming throughput for stable heavy routes. We prefer a short-lived local mitigation that preserves client-perceived availability while we iterate on longer-term regional affinity fixes.
- Rescue is opt-in behind a feature flag (router.flags.rescue.enabled) to allow fast rollback if we see unintended regressions.

CI and validation:
- CI initially failed due to a flake in probe hedging UTs (race during test teardown). Fixed by adding deterministic clock and explicit probe cancellation.
- Full test matrix (unit + integration) ran in ~22m on CI; perf-canary integration against a staging cluster showed 45% reduction in 99.9th percentile tail latency for affected routes during synthetic cross-region spike. Memory/CPU increase <4% observed on serving nodes.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI. Post-merge we kicked a staging canary and watched rescue_active_routes spike and slo_violation drop for the affected customers. Ops has the flag ready to toggle.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-10012: Integrate rescue signals into regional failover planner to make rescues trigger coordinated region handoffs instead of local isolation (medium term).
- Dashboard follow-up to create a permanent panel that cross-correlates rescue_sessions with slo_violation_by_tenant.

review_conversation: Carlos Rivera: Can't we just increase the cooldown globally? Concern is cross-tenant impact if rescue misfires.

Maya Thompson: We considered a global cooldown but that adds latency for healthy tenants; rescue is per-route and opt-in so scope is limited. Added explanation and default limits in the PR description.
Anika Patel: Request: add an explicit metric for trims_by_tenant so SRE can attribute regressions quickly.
Maya Thompson: Added trimmed_token_count and labeled it by tenant and route. Also added tests that assert metric emission on trim events.

Liam O'Connor: Found a potential race in hedged_probe teardown. Reproducer attached.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after the deterministic clock fix and test update.
Maya Thompson: Addressed the race by injecting a cancellable context and deterministic clock in tests; pushed fix and re-ran CI.
ops_runbook_note: If rescue causes unexpected throughput loss toggle router.flags.rescue.enabled=false. Monitor rescue_active_routes and trimmed_token_count for rollback verification. Contact on-call SRE if SLOs increase after rollback.
